svg.title: PCA in a RAG vector index: orthogonal projection from 3D to 2D
svg.desc: Left: embeddings scattered around a tilted plane in a three-dimensional space, drawn over the reference xy plane. Right: the same vectors projected orthogonally onto that plane. The ring around each projected point shows the distance from the plane that the projection discards, which is the approximation error.
svg.text: Embeddings of the vector index scatter around a tilted plane (n = 3)
Same vectors in the plane (k = 2); the distance from the plane is lost
The approximation error is the component of x orthogonal to the principal subspace, the ring radius in the plane.
On average it equals the discarded variance, Σ λᵢ for i > k, and it can push a relevant chunk out of the RAG retriever's top-K.
